review_status: Author-selected lexical hypotheses from top500 separate TRAIN frequencies, before new evaluation selection. Not native bilingual certification.
selection_policy: Prefer ordinary content concepts and independently attested complete target words. Synonyms are not ambiguity by themselves. Exclude obvious common sense/POS splits such as like, right, cool, fan, book and work. Rare metaphorical or verb uses of ordinary nouns remain a measured risk. No full-sentence translation agreement is required.
known_risks_to_score: Idioms can change the meaning of otherwise ordinary content words.
Rare noun/verb homographs, metaphors, names written lowercase, and unknown context can defeat context-independent lookup.
Explicit infinitives are complete attested words but native grammar mixed with them can be awkward; distinguish mild hybrid grammar from material tense/meaning loss.
Function words can have pragmatic or grammatical constraints; function-only success must not be presented as content-vocabulary coverage.
Some nouns have singular/plural surface identity in Swahili; preserve reviewed actual forms, never Roman class labels from malformed extraction metadata.

pre_holdout_review_rejections.son: mwana source explicitly includes son or daughter; do not discard male distinction in a supposedly low-ambiguity mapping.
pre_holdout_review_rejections.never: kamwe source includes ever and never; polarity depends on surrounding grammar, which this context-independent baseline cannot supply.
pre_holdout_review_rejections.man: Common conversational interjection and generic-person uses make the proposed literal male-person mapping unsuitable for this small baseline.
